In [geometry](/wiki/Geometry "Geometry"), a **pentagonal trapezohedron** is the third in the infinite family of [trapezohedra](/wiki/Trapezohedra "Trapezohedra"), face-transitive polyhedra. Its [dual polyhedron](/wiki/Dual_polyhedron "Dual polyhedron") is the [pentagonal antiprism](/wiki/Pentagonal_antiprism "Pentagonal antiprism"). As a [decahedron](/wiki/Decahedron "Decahedron") it has ten faces which are [congruent](/wiki/Congruence_(geometry) "Congruence (geometry)") [kites](/wiki/Kite_(geometry) "Kite (geometry)").

One particular pentagonal trapezohedron can be decomposed into two [pentagonal pyramids](/wiki/Pentagonal_pyramid "Pentagonal pyramid") and a [regular dodecahedron](/wiki/Regular_dodecahedron "Regular dodecahedron") in the middle.[[1]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAlsinaNelsen2020[httpsbooksgooglecombooksidCGDSDwAAQBAJpgPA75_75]-1)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/04/Pentagonal_trapezohedron.stl/250px-Pentagonal_trapezohedron.stl.png)](/wiki/File:Pentagonal_trapezohedron.stl)

3D model of a pentagonal trapezohedron

The pentagonal trapezohedron has ten quadrilaterals, twenty edges, and 12 vertices. Each face is a [kite](/wiki/Kite_(geometry) "Kite (geometry)"), with one version having its three interior angles at 108° and one interior angle at 36°. Truncating both top and bottom vertices of this polyhedron achieves the [regular dodecahedron](/wiki/Regular_dodecahedron "Regular dodecahedron").[[2]](#cite_note-2)

In recent years, with the advent of technologies such as [Statcast](/wiki/Statcast "Statcast") and its use of [Hawk-Eye](/wiki/Hawk-Eye "Hawk-Eye") starting in 2020[[91]](#cite_note-92) as well as with advanced statistics as provided by sites such as [FanGraphs](/wiki/FanGraphs "FanGraphs") and Baseball Savant, MLB has evolved. With the ability to see precise movements of pitchers and batters, teams can assess the mechanics of a player and help them improve. Statcast also provides some features such as tracking the paths of most batted balls, tracking the speed of most batted balls, and tracking the [exit velocity](/wiki/Exit_velocity "Exit velocity") of most batted balls. Statcast has allowed for advanced defensive analytics that have not been possible before tracking of players due to how subjective fielding can be.

The rate of teams using a [defensive shift](/wiki/Defensive_shift "Defensive shift") went up from 13.7% in 2016 to 33.6% in 2022 because advanced statistics supported this as an effective way to stop hitters from getting hits.[[92]](#cite_note-93) Because the shift reduces the number of balls in play that result in hits and MLB wishes to increase interest in baseball, MLB announced in September 2022 that extreme infield defensive shifts would be banned starting in 2023. To be compliant, there must be two fielders on each side of second base, and those fielders must have both of their feet on the infield dirt at the time the pitch is thrown. If this rule is not followed, the choice of an automatic ball or the outcome of the play is given to the batting team.[[93]](#cite_note-:0-94)

The game of baseball has also slowed down significantly due to an increased number of strikeouts and walks—two outcomes that generally take many pitches to complete—and an increased amount of time taken for a pitcher to pitch.
